title: MZ Riftworld MZ - A Fantasy RPG Sim

posts.author: Philly
posts.body:
I’ve been working with
RPG Maker
for a very long time – starting all the way back with
RPG Maker 95
and continuing up to
RPG Maker MZ
today. According to Steam, I’m about to hit
6,000 hours
with MZ alone.
For quite some time now, I’ve also been working on a game that I’d like to
release commercially
at some point. Recently, I replayed
Ultima VII
and
Ultima Underworld
(both available on GOG), and that made me ask myself a simple question:
Why are there no good RPG Sims anymore?
I mean,
Morrowind
and
Skyrim
(which are already considered “old” by today’s standards) were excellent RPG Sims as well. Where are the games where you can simply wander through the world and focus on other things? Blacksmithing, tailoring, alchemy. Doing side quests, exploring regions and caves. Sitting in a tavern and doing absolutely nothing.
Sure, there have been many great RPGs and JRPGs – for example
Baldur’s Gate 3
or
Clair Obscur
. But somehow I really miss proper RPG Sims where you can do
everything
— except being forced to follow the main story.
Kenshi
still exists, of course, but Kenshi is very much its own special case.
Rune Factory
also comes to mind, but even there nothing truly new has appeared in a long time. New entries tend to feel more like DLC than full evolutions.
While thinking about all this, I came to the conclusion that maybe I should simply try to create an RPG Sim myself – using
RPG Maker MZ
.
When the latest MZ update was released, I didn’t hesitate for a second. I started the Maker, selected the template with hundreds of prebuilt maps (wtf?), and began working on a concept. By the way, I’d really like to thank the person who created almost
200 maps
for that template.
Seriously — thank you! You’re insane  (in a good way).
Anyway, back to the point.
I started a new project, suddenly had nearly 200 ready-made maps, and a clear goal in mind:
to create an
ULTIMATE RPG SIM
.
The project already has a name:
Riftworld MZ
. Yes, it’s uncreative and boring — but it’s just a working title for now.
So what exactly is my concept?
First and foremost, I want the player to have
as much freedom as possible
. That means little to no artificial barriers. For example, no invisible walls that prevent the player from entering certain areas. Instead, almost every location can be reached freely.
Players can ignore the story and take on quests, go fishing, gather resources, buy and decorate property, summon heroes from a completely unnecessary gacha system (just because — thanks to Undermax for that plugin ), fight in an arena, open a bank account, craft epic equipment, cook, play minigames, visit casinos, and much more.
All of this takes place in an immersive world featuring a
day/night cycle
and
dynamic weather
.
There
is
a red thread, but it’s designed in such a loose way that players can easily spend
dozens of hours
before ever touching the main quest.
Here’s the rough story idea I currently have in mind:
Elotria
is a classic fantasy world with multiple kingdoms, continents, and so on. About 300 years ago, portals appeared all across the planet, unleashing monsters into the world. A great war followed, but in the end, the peoples of Elotria were victorious.
Three centuries later, the
Explorer Guild
exists — an organization dedicated to exploring portals, dungeons, and other dangerous locations. We join this guild and become an Explorer ourselves.
To avoid dying out there, players can currently choose from
38 different jobs
, each offering unique abilities.
When it comes to skills: class-specific skills are learned via the
VisuStella Skill Learn System
. Additionally, techniques and magic can be purchased and learned separately. A mage can learn techniques, and a warrior can learn magic — but only after unlocking the respective systems first.
As a result, even a barbarian might end up throwing fireballs, or a mage practicing kung fu.
That’s how I imagine an RPG Sim made with RPG Maker.
Now I’m wondering:
Is there actually any interest in a game like this?
It’s definitely a lot of work. People usually estimate about 100 hours of development time for one hour of gameplay, so this is a project that will probably keep me busy for several years. And I’m only working on it on the side - I still have a main project. I just wanted to share my ideas with you. Do you maybe have any ideas or suggestions?

posts.author: TotalyNate
posts.body: I love the idea of a chill, open world rpg with a turn-based battle system, especially one that doesnt focus on the main plot to much. Seems like the kind of game I would play for an ungodly amount of time if it existed.

posts.author: Philly
posts.body:
Small update. I’m spending a lot of time in the database right now. At the moment, I’m working on ores that we can mine. The ores are divided into T1–T7. I’m currently thinking about whether we should first process the ores into ingots to forge equipment, or use the ores directly.
I’m also working on the job system. At the start of the game, we can choose one of five base classes. After that, we’ll need JP and possibly items. I’m considering adding trainers as well. We would have to complete a small quest for a trainer to earn a job certificate. With this certificate, we could then learn a new job. Also, only the player character will be able to change jobs.
